# Glossary

Terms as the legacy code uses them. Where code vocabulary might not match how support/users talk
about the system, that gap is called out — those gaps are candidate ASK material if a future
phase needs to resolve them, but none currently block a work order.

| term | code meaning | notes |
|---|---|---|
| **ticket** | a row in `tickets` | Standard usage, no conflict expected. |
| **slug** | `slugify(title)` output — lowercase, alnum-and-hyphens, ≤64 chars | Code treats this as a derived display value, not an identifier — `GET`/`close` route by numeric `id`, never by slug. If support or the UI treats the slug as if it were a stable per-ticket identifier (plausible, given PB-003 exists — collisions matter more if two things wrongly count as "the same"), that's a code-vocabulary/user-vocabulary gap worth surfacing to whoever rules OQ-001. |
| **priority** | one of `low`/`med`/`high`, stored as text; API accepts `1`/`2`/`3` as synonyms | The int-to-word mapping (`server.py:47-49`) suggests two client populations historically sent different shapes — worth knowing if the new stack should keep both or the UI-freeze (PB-006) settles it by definition (UI keeps sending whatever it sends today, so both stay). |
| **status** (ticket) | `open` \| `closed`, DB-enforced | No "in progress," "blocked," "resolved-not-closed," etc. — a genuinely two-state model. If support's mental model has more states, that's not evidenced anywhere in the code and isn't in scope to invent. |
| **watchers** | the fixed recipient address `watchers@example.internal` (`server.py:76`) — hardcoded, not a table, not a per-ticket list | Despite the name, there is no `watchers` entity/table anywhere — every ticket-close notification goes to the same single address regardless of ticket content. Worth flagging: if "watchers" implies per-ticket subscribers in how people talk about the product, the code does not implement that at all. Not a PB entry (nobody reported this as wrong), just recorded so the rewrite doesn't accidentally *build* a per-ticket watcher feature under the assumption it already existed. |
| **reset token** | see `docs/domain/reset_token.md` | Bearer credential for the password-reset flow; despite the name nothing in this codebase implements passwords or a login flow at all — "reset" resets nothing observable in this system (no `users.password` field exists). The token's only observable effect is being deletable via `confirm_reset`. This system may be intentionally decoupled from a separate auth service that owns actual passwords — not evidenced either way, see OQ-007. |
| **internal** (as in `/internal/export/csv`) | a route path prefix, not an enforced access-control boundary — no auth middleware exists anywhere in this app | Naming implies restricted access; nothing in the code restricts it. Same trust model as every other route (see OQ-007). |
